bug_semantics: The GDS Flask application exposes command, telemetry/event history, file-upload/download, destination-selection, sequence, and optional log endpoints without authenticating or authorizing the HTTP caller. The documented constant 0xfeedcafe on command and sequence requests is only a publicly disclosed accidental-action guard, not proof of identity. When the GUI listener is made network-reachable, an unauthenticated caller can select a command and arguments and reach pipeline.send_command, as well as invoke the file/sequence operations, producing the command-injection and host-impact exposure described by CVE-2026-72577.
flaw_origin: c632f1ab5c071a708ada5aeb7a5a969ea41a68ec is the smallest root BIC: it created src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py and src/fprime_gds/flask/commands.py and directly attached /commands, /commands/<command>, /events, and /channels to a Flask-RESTful API with no authentication middleware, session validation, principal, or authorization check. The direct parent contains neither file. ebe1a7062dba9d7e7d3c486757b042136f9015d0 later connected the command resource to the pipeline and added sender.send_command(command, arg_list), and later commits added upload/sequence endpoints, but those changes expanded/activated impact while inheriting the already-established no-authentication architecture rather than introducing its root cause.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names author Michael D Starch <Michael.D.Starch@jpl.nasa.gov> and committer Michael D Starch <Michael.D.Starch@jpl.nasa.gov>; its complete message is "mstarch: initial implementation of REST API for ETC" and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot marker.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p6w2-c4j5-7xhm and https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-72577 identify CWE-306, state that fprime-gds through 3.4.3 permits unauthenticated RCE/spacecraft command injection, and specifically identify src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py as applying no authentication. GitHub lists affected and patched versions as Unknown and no source-code fix.

BIC: https://github.com/nasa/fprime-gds/commit/c632f1ab5c071a708ada5aeb7a5a969ea41a68ec. `git log --all --follow --name-status -- src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py` ends at this commit with status A. Its patch creates app.py lines 20-34 with `app = flask.Flask(__name__)`, `api = flask_restful.Api(app)`, and unguarded route registrations including `/commands/<command>`; it simultaneously creates commands.py lines 54-73 with the command PUT resource and publicly documented 0xfeedcafe guard. Commit-specific source: https://github.com/nasa/fprime-gds/blob/c632f1ab5c071a708ada5aeb7a5a969ea41a68ec/src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py and https://github.com/nasa/fprime-gds/blob/c632f1ab5c071a708ada5aeb7a5a969ea41a68ec/src/fprime_gds/flask/commands.py.

Direct-parent verification: raw BIC object gives sole parent 7551706a0a8352876e64244fed4941acea2a6f0c. Both `git cat-file -e 7551706a0a8352876e64244fed4941acea2a6f0c:src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py` and the equivalent commands.py check fail with `path ... exists on disk, but not in` that parent, proving the vulnerable Flask API files/route table are absent. Parent: https://github.com/nasa/fprime-gds/commit/7551706a0a8352876e64244fed4941acea2a6f0c; creation diff: https://github.com/nasa/fprime-gds/compare/7551706a0a8352876e64244fed4941acea2a6f0c...c632f1ab5c071a708ada5aeb7a5a969ea41a68ec.

Impact activation without changing the root BIC: https://github.com/nasa/fprime-gds/commit/ebe1a7062dba9d7e7d3c486757b042136f9015d0 changes app.py to pass the pipeline into the still-unguarded command resource and adds `self.sender.send_command(command, arg_list)` in commands.py; `git grep send_command ebe1a706...^ -- src/fprime_gds/flask/commands.py` returns no match. Current commands.py lines 72-96 still accepts the public key and calls send_command without any caller identity check.

Version membership: `git tag --contains c632f1ab5c071a7085a969ea41a68ec` (full command used the complete SHA c632f1ab5c071a708ada5aeb7a5a969ea41a68ec) lists every repository release tag from 2.0 through v4.3.0, including the advisory boundary v3.4.3. Release points are 2.0 at 0b2879a09a3b4f7e489ea2076188c0c0bfa99f43 (2021-06-14), v3.4.3 at 7f3bb470f55f9d8559c00141b6790580345ac05e (2024-02-16), and v4.3.0 at fbcb6e7cffc85a82f99557c3258593ed89449430 (2026-08-19).

Affected boundary source checks: `git show 2.0:src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py` already shows unguarded command and upload route registration. `git show v3.4.3:src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py` shows the same unguarded `/commands/<command>`, `/upload/destination`, `/upload/files`, `/download/files`, and `/sequence` resources. Review URL: https://github.com/nasa/fprime-gds/blob/v3.4.3/src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py.

Unpatched/fixed-boundary check: the clone HEAD equals v4.3.0 (fbcb6e7cffc85a82f99557c3258593ed89449430), and `git show v4.3.0:src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py` still registers all sensitive resources without authentication; a history search for `before_request` and a broader -G search for `login_required|Authorization|before_request|authenticat` in src/fprime_gds/flask found no authentication implementation. Review URL: https://github.com/nasa/fprime-gds/blob/v4.3.0/src/fprime_gds/flask/app.py. PyPI reports 4.3.0 as latest: https://pypi.org/project/fprime-gds/. Therefore there is no fix commit, direct fix, or patched-version boundary in the available public history; the advisory's 'through 3.4.3' wording is underinclusive relative to the repository and latest published package.

BIC-only AI attribution: `git cat-file -p c632f1ab5c071a708ada5aeb7a5a969ea41a68ec` yields tree e2760c6a57657342188ee1d2232e1894dedaed9b, parent 7551706a0a8352876e64244fed4941acea2a6f0c, human author/committer Michael D Starch, and only the one-line message; no trailer or bot identity is present. No later commit, PR, branch, or fix attribution was used for the verdict.
reasoning: The advisory's shared causal defect is not a particular upload parser or command serializer; it is that the Flask API was created without any authentication boundary around sensitive resources. History tracing shows the app and its first unguarded route table originate together in c632f1ab5c071a708ada5aeb7a5a969ea41a68ec, while direct inspection of its sole parent proves both relevant Flask files are absent there. That makes c632 the earliest non-move, non-refactor root BIC. The later ebe1a7062dba9d7e7d3c486757b042136f9015d0 commit made unauthenticated command dispatch operational, and later upload/sequence work enlarged the attack surface, but neither supplied the missing authentication boundary. The BIC precedes every repository release tag: the vulnerable design is present in 2.0 and the reported v3.4.3 boundary. It remains present in v4.3.0, which is both HEAD and the latest PyPI release, so this case is explicitly unpatched and fix_sha/direct_fix_sha are null. Finally, the BIC commit object has only a named human author/committer and no AI/bot trailer or identity; under BIC-only attribution, the correct closed verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched: no public fix SHA, direct remediation commit, or patched-version boundary exists through repository/PyPI release v4.3.0; a future remediation cannot yet be audited.

unpatched.reason: No public fix SHA, direct remediation commit, or patched-version boundary exists through repository/PyPI release v4.3.0.

potential_fix.approach: Add authentication/authorization middleware to the GDS Flask routes (command, telemetry, file up/download, sequence, logs) and bind the web server to a non-public interface by default.
potential_fix.rationale: Requiring authenticated, authorized sessions on every exposed operational endpoint closes the unauthenticated control surface.
